newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Mercenary group ends Sierra Leone mission.
newsitem.headline: Mercenary group ends Sierra Leone mission.

text.p: South African mercenary group Executive Outcomes has left Sierra Leone after helping turn the tide in its civil war by backing the army against rebels.

"Executive Outcomes has officially left Sierra Leone," the group's commander, Brigadier Burt Sachse told Reuters on Tuesday. He said a planeload of employees left on Monday and only a handful of people were staying behind to wind down the accounts.

The group has been in Sierra Leone since May 1995. The then military government in Freetown turned to the Pretoria-based firm after rebels who took up arms in 1991 overran key bauxite and diamond mining centres and attacked close to the capital.

At the height of their operations the mercenaries numbered about 300 and included some fighters from Angola, where the group first backed UNITA rebels and then the government army. Military sources said the number fell to about 30 by the end.

The mercenaries helped train the West African country's army, which retook the initiative in the war and forced Revolutionary United Front rebels to negotiate. Executive Outcomes also assured security at important mining sites.
Although a U.N. force of about 700 is due to monitor the accord, security worries loom again in Sierra Leone after the government's announcement of three coup plots in four months.
Amid allegations of truce violations by the government and rebels, mining companies who braved the civil war and stayed are considering alternative security arrangements.
Sachse, however, sounded optimistic when asked last month about the departure of Executive Outcomes, a key demand of the rebels that blocked negotiations for months.

"There is no longer a requirement for an offensive force in the land," he told Reuters. "I believe the government is quite capable of handling its own internal security problem. We must now leave the country".
President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who took office in March 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule, agreed a peace deal with rebel leader Foday Sankoh in Ivory Coast in December.
Controversy has dogged the activities of Executive Outcomes in Sierra Leone and elsewhere in Africa.

Executive Outcomes has denied sending men to join a mercenary force helping the Zaire army against rebels in the east but sources close to the group acknowledge that some of the South Africans who were in Sierra Leone are now in Zaire, not as Executive Outcomes but as members of other security outfits.

Donors expected to fund Sierra Leone's reconstruction and rehabilitation queried the millions of dollars paid by the state to the group. Sierra Leone is widely believed to have settled part of the bill through mining concessions.
